$description: Voice and content rules. Not visual tokens — these govern strings, and they are here so a linter and a reviewer can both cite them.

casing.rule: Sentence case for everything a person reads: buttons, form labels, headings, navigation, dialog titles, menu items, empty states, tooltips.
casing.capitals: First letter and proper nouns only (GitHub, Claude, Bindery, Acme Corp).
casing.exception: The 11px uppercase micro-label is a CSS text-transform treatment, not a casing rule. The source string stays sentence case so it stays translatable. Never type an uppercase string.

date.relative: Up to 7 days: just now · 14 minutes ago · 2 hours ago · yesterday.
date.absolute: After 7 days: 12 Aug (this year) · 12 Aug 2025 (other years).
date.full: 12 Aug 2026, 14:32 — used in detail views and in the title attribute of every relative time.
date.rule: The month is always a word. Pin the options and let the locale choose the order. Never call toLocaleDateString() bare; never hard-code a locale.
date.audit: 31 bare toLocale*() calls across the four apps; exactly one passes options.

number.bytes: base-1024 maths with KB/MB/GB labels; 1 decimal below 10, 0 above — 8.0 MB, 54.8 MB, 311 KB
number.durationMs: under 1s show ms — 184 ms, never 0.18 s
number.durationS: under 60s show one decimal — 2.4 s; over a minute use m:ss — 3:07
number.currency: no rule yet — none of the four apps handles money. When one does: Intl.NumberFormat with the currency code shown for anything that is not the user's own.
number.audit: 23 references to 1024 and four different toFixed precisions (0, 1, 2, 4) across the apps.

structure: what to do next — as a control, not a sentence
never: an internal identifier: parameter name, class name, key type
blaming the user — describe the state instead
a dead end with no next action where one exists

structure: a heading naming what is absent
an action, if one genuinely exists
emptyState.never: "No items" — that is a status code, not an empty state.
emptyState.distinguish: nothing exists yet vs nothing matched the filter — different situations, different next steps. The four apps currently render both as "No items".

button.rule: Verb first; object when it is not obvious from context.
button.destructive: Name the object and the count — "Dismiss 3 items", never "Confirm". The count is the last chance to notice the wrong rows are selected.
never: Yes / No on a destructive dialog
a bare "Save" where the object is unclear

forbidden.Oops / Whoops / Uh oh: Something failed and the interface is being cute about it.
forbidden.Simply, just, easy: If it were simple the user would not be reading an instruction.
forbidden.Are you sure?: Almost always. Say what will happen instead.
forbidden.Invalid: A judgement, not a description. Say what was expected.
forbidden.Error occurred: Every error occurred. Say which one.
forbidden.Loading\u2026 as a lone state: Use a skeleton of the thing being loaded.

$extensions.d3.implementation: The date, byte, duration and percentage formatters are a single shared module. Signatures are fixed here; the implementation lands in Phase 5 with the components, per the no-production-code-before-Phase-5 rule.
